caveats: **Per-user installs on Windows appear only in `list_per_user`.** `list`, `query` and `list_inventory` read the machine keys and the agent account's own user key, so an application installed for one user is not in them. In `list_per_user`, a missing privilege, a truncated profile list or a hive that fails to unload is reported by a warning row only, with the typed status still `UNDECLARED`, so check the rows and not just the status.

**Windows hive reads degrade loudly, with one benign exception.** A missing user or 32-bit Uninstall key is normal and ignored; any other open or enumeration failure, an over-long subkey name or an application key whose open fails marks the walk degraded while the apps already read are kept. A `DisplayName` that is not a string, or is over 64 KiB, is read as empty and that entry is skipped without a degraded mark, and a subkey deleted during enumeration can hide a sibling.

**macOS `signature_status` is presence, not validity.** The enrichment reads the code-signing information only and never checks the signature, so a bundle with its `_CodeSignature` removed or with bytes appended still reads `signed`, and `publisher` is then unverified attribution. Deep verification is deliberately not performed.

**A failed read is withheld, and macOS `list_inventory` is cached.** A killed, timed-out, truncated or non-zero-exit tool makes the action emit an `error|` row and return rc 1 rather than a partial list, and the daily sync then skips that cycle. macOS `list_inventory` reuses its `system_profiler` scan for 10 minutes unless the Applications or receipt directories change, and a degraded or empty scan is never cached.

**`install_location` and `bundle_id` are untrusted.** Both are as the local bundle or installer reports them, so a local user can plant a bundle whose identifier is any string, and `install_location` can sit under a user's home. On Windows a product registered in more than one hive keeps the first record's fields and the smallest populated `InstallLocation`; on Linux both columns are always `-`.

definitions.description: Enumerates all installed applications on the endpoint. On Windows, reads the registry Uninstall keys (64-bit HKLM, 32-bit WoW64, and HKCU), and deduplicates by name+version (the `SystemComponent` filter is inert today -- the value is a REG_DWORD the string reader rejects -- and is a tracked follow-up). The HKCU read is the AGENT SERVICE ACCOUNT's own hive, not a logged-in user's: the agent runs as a system-context service (LocalSystem today, see #1442), so HKCU resolves to that account's profile and carries no end-user applications. This is deliberate machine scope, not a gap -- per-user applications are a separate action (list_per_user) that this one never invokes. On Linux, auto-detects the package manager (dpkg, rpm, or pacman). On macOS, queries system_profiler for GUI applications. Returns application name, version, publisher, install date, install location, and (macOS) bundle identifier. Rows are seven escape-aware tokens (every field: `\` to `/`, `|` to `\|`, CR/LF to a space, over 4 KiB cut); split on an unescaped `|`. The dashboard results table shows this definition's rows as key/value (app plus one remainder cell); read the six columns positionally from the raw output on the REST/MCP response routes. Agents older than plugin 1.2.0 emit five tokens and do NOT escape `|` in name, version, publisher or install date, so such a row can split into any count: accept a row only when it has exactly 5 or exactly 7 tokens under the escape-aware split, reject any other count, and read the sixth and seventh columns only for agents known to run plugin 1.2.0 or later. A macOS list may lead with a warning|bundle_id_* row; ignore lines whose first token is not app.

Enumerates installed applications on a per-user basis. On Windows, iterates user profiles and reads each user's Software\Microsoft\Windows\CurrentVersion\Uninstall -- from the LIVE HKEY_USERS\<SID> hive when that user is logged in, falling back to an offline mount of their NTUSER.DAT only when it is not loaded. On Linux, reports system-wide packages (dpkg/rpm). On macOS, reports system apps plus per-user Homebrew packages. Output includes the username (or "system") alongside each application record.

Searches for a specific installed application by case-insensitive partial name match. Returns a found/not-found indicator followed by matching application records. Useful for compliance checks (e.g. verifying a required security agent is installed) and license auditing.

description: Inventories installed applications and queries by name
how_it_works:
`installed_apps` answers "what software is on this device" from the operating system's own records and never installs, removes or verifies anything. Four actions share one set of OS readers. `list` returns one `app|` row per application: Windows reads the Uninstall registry keys (64-bit and 32-bit machine keys, plus the agent account's own user key); Linux uses the first package manager it finds (`dpkg-query`, else `rpm`, else `pacman`); macOS runs `system_profiler SPApplicationsDataType` for GUI applications and then reads each bundle's identifier in one bounded pass. `query` takes the same collection and returns the rows whose name contains the given text (case-insensitive), preceded by `found|true` or followed by only `found|false`. `list_per_user` is the per-person view: on Windows it walks every local profile's registry hive; on Linux and macOS it returns the same system-wide set tagged `system` (plus Homebrew formulae tagged `brew` on macOS). `list_inventory` is a separate, richer collector for the daily sync: it has no instruction definition, so it is not offered to operators; the agent's daily sync runs it.

If the OS reader fails part-way (a tool is killed, times out, exits non-zero or is truncated, or a Windows Uninstall key cannot be read to the end), `list`, `query` and `list_inventory` return an `error|` row (or nothing, for `list_inventory`) and rc 1 instead of a short list, so a partial result is never mistaken for a complete one. A genuinely empty `list` is a single `app|No applications found` row.

columns.description: Where the application lives on disk, as the OS reports it. Windows: the Uninstall key's InstallLocation value, returned raw — a REG_EXPAND_SZ value such as %ProgramFiles%\Vendor is NOT expanded — or "-" when the value is absent (many MSI-registered products, SDK/runtime component packages and NSIS/portable installers write none — 182 of 241 rows on one developer workstation), longer than 64 KiB (the registry reader's bound; a value between 4 KiB and 64 KiB is cut to 4 KiB at a character boundary), or not a string type. Applications installed only into a logged-in user's own hive are not listed by this machine-scope action at all (use list_per_user); entries in the agent service account's own HKCU Uninstall key keep their InstallLocation. Where the same product is registered in more than one hive the smallest populated value wins. Unlike windows.software.msi.list, separators are "/": backslashes are emitted as "/" (a UNC path reads //srv/share; not reversible), so C:\Program Files\7-Zip\ reads C:/Program Files/7-Zip/. macOS: the location system_profiler reports, normally the .app bundle path and occasionally a non-bundle directory; this can lie under a user's home (/Users/<account>/...). Always "-" on Linux by design: a package installs files to many prefixes, so there is no single install location. Values: path or "-". The value is as reported by the OS: untrusted and non-canonical.
columns.name: install_location

columns.description: The macOS CFBundleIdentifier read in-process from the bundle at install_location (reverse-DNS form). Always "-" on Windows and Linux, which have no bundle identifier concept; "-" on macOS when the location is not a bundle or carries no identifier, and for rows the bounded bundle-id pass did not reach (30 s deadline, at most 5000 applications submitted, one pass in flight per agent process (one per device)) -- a cut-short or capped pass is reported by a leading warning|bundle_id_* row and a CONSTRAINED / PARTIAL status, never silently. An identifier is cut at 4 KiB at read. The value is as reported by the OS: untrusted, as reported by the local bundle — a local user can plant a bundle whose identifier is any string. Values: bundle identifier or "-".

outputs_note:
Pipe-delimited rows, one per application, written via `write_output()`. `list`/`query`/`list_per_user` emit the stable `app`/`app`/`user_app`-tagged wire format `content/definitions/installed_apps.yaml` documents; `-` marks a field the OS reported empty or one that does not apply on that OS (`install_location`/`bundle_id` on Linux, `bundle_id` on Windows). `list_inventory` emits a separate, extended `inv`-tagged 13-token row (blob contract v2, ADR-0016) where a field an ecosystem does not store stays *honestly empty* — never a `-` placeholder. Every `list` field is escape-aware (`format_app_row`): `\` folds to `/`, `|` becomes `\|`, CR/LF become a space, an interior NUL cuts the field, a field over 4 KiB is cut; `query`/`list_per_user` rows are raw but bounded: every registry-sourced field is cut at 4 KiB at read (Windows), so a hostile registry string cannot inflate them.

**Server rendering.** `installed_apps` is one of the server's key/value plugins (`kKeyValuePlugins`, `server/core/src/result_parsing.hpp`), so the dashboard results table, its detail drawer, sort and facets split every row at the first pipe only — `app` plus one remainder cell — whatever columns the definition declares; `install_location` and `bundle_id`, like `version`/`publisher`/`install_date` before them, are not separately rendered, sortable or filterable there. `GET /api/v1/responses/{id}` (and its export) and MCP `query_responses` return the raw seven-token row in `output`, which is where automation should read the columns. The server splits these rows at the first pipe only; a definition-aware splitter does not exist yet.

**Parsing `list` rows.** `app|name|version|publisher|install_date|install_location|bundle_id` — seven escape-aware tokens. Split `output` on newlines first (one response can carry many rows); split each line on `|` not preceded by `\`, then decode `\|` to `|`; `\` never otherwise appears (folded to `/`, which makes a UNC path `//srv/share` and is not reversible), CR/LF are folded to a space, and the raw value is cut at 4 KiB before escaping, so an emitted field can be up to 8 KiB. `-` means empty or not applicable. A macOS `list` may lead with a `warning|bundle_id_*` row; ignore lines whose first token is not `app`. Agents older than plugin 1.2.0 emit five tokens and do not escape `|`, so a row from one can split into any count: accept a row only when it has exactly 5 or exactly 7 tokens under the escape-aware split, reject any other count, and read the sixth/seventh columns only for agents known to be on plugin >= 1.2.0. REST and MCP return this text verbatim; only the dashboard decodes `\|`, inside its merged cell.



**Empty-result convention.** `list` with nothing to report returns a single `app` row named `No applications found`. `list_inventory` drops a row outright if `name` is empty and has no sentinel row, so an empty collection is empty output at rc 0. A *degraded* collection instead returns rc 1 and the daily sync skips the whole cycle rather than committing a partial inventory as authoritative.

privileges.grant: **None** for `list`, `query` and `list_inventory`: `Reg*W` reads only. `list_per_user`'s offline `NTUSER.DAT` mount for a logged-out profile uses `SeBackupPrivilege` and `SeRestorePrivilege`, which the agent account already holds.
privileges.if_refused: `list_per_user` writes `warning|privilege_missing: ...` naming how many logged-out profiles could not be read, `warning|hive_file_refused` per refused hive and `warning|hive_read_failed` for unreadable Uninstall keys; machine-scope actions are unaffected. An unreadable profile list is `error|profile_list_unreadable` with rc 1.

result_status.when: a degraded acquisition (Linux/macOS: a subprocess that failed to start, exited nonzero, was killed, timed out or was truncated; Windows: an Uninstall root that could not be opened or enumerated to the end, or an application subkey whose open failed): `list`, `query` and `list_inventory` return rc 1, and so does `list_per_user` on Linux and macOS

Windows `list_per_user`: one or more profiles' Uninstall key could not be read (a trailing `warning|hive_read_failed` row counts the profiles), or a profile's hive file was refused by the offline guard (a trailing `warning|hive_file_refused` row names the SID and the guard's token); the rows already read stay, rc 0
macOS `list`: the 30 s bundle-id pass deadline hit; a leading `warning|bundle_id_timeout` row, unread rows carry `-`, rc 0
macOS `list`: another bundle-id pass is in flight on this device (a concurrent `list` or an earlier abandoned pass); all rows carry `-`, rc 0
macOS `list`: the bounded-call ceiling refused the pass or its admission allocation failed; all rows carry `-`, rc 0
macOS `list`: more than 5000 located apps, only the first 5000 submitted; the rest carry `-`, rc 0; a timed-out, busy or rejected pass outranks this warning and status

every other run, healthy or not: the wire stays `UNDECLARED` and the agent log derives `OK` from rc 0. This includes Windows `list_per_user` runs that end with only a `warning|privilege_missing`, a profile-list truncation warning or a hive-unload warning (row text only, rc 0), and the `error|profile_list_unreadable` failure (rc 1)

where_the_data_goes: **Instruction result.** `list`/`query`/`list_per_user` rows travel over the agent's mTLS gRPC channel as the command response and land in the ResponseStore (operator-configurable retention, 90-day default), queryable at `/api/v1/responses/{id}`.

**Daily-sync typed store.** `list_inventory` is never dispatched through `execute_instruction` — it has no definition. The agent's own `SyncSource` (`make_installed_software_source` in `sync_source_installed_software.cpp`) runs it every 24 hours, canonicalizes the parsed rows into a hash-skip blob, and pushes it to the server's typed `SoftwareInventoryStore` (ADR-0016), served fleet-wide at `GET /api/v1/inventory/software` gated on `Inventory:Read`.
**Not consumed by** TAR, DEX, or metrics — no reference to `installed_apps`/`crossplatform.software.*` was found in the TAR or DEX collector sources.

**Sensitivity.** `list_per_user`/`list_inventory` rows carry per-account software names/versions/publishers, and `list_per_user`'s `username` field is a resolved local account name (not a raw SID) — a per-person installed-software inventory; `list`/`query`/`list_inventory` alone already name specific installed software (`name`/`version`/`publisher`) even at machine scope. `list`'s `install_location` names a user's home directory when an application is installed under it (`/Users/<account>/Applications/…`, `/Users/<account>/Library/…` — 4 of 323 rows in the macOS capture), or `C:/Users/<name>/...` on Windows; the macOS count is from an unprivileged capture — the root daemon may list every account's `~/Applications`; the committed sample redacts the account to `jsmith`.

**Siblings:** `msi_packages.*` (Windows-only MSI package detail) and `license_scan.list` (software-licence/entitlement detection) — grouped alongside `installed_apps` in the privilege model's read-only row (`docs/agent-privilege-model.md`).

**MCP / REST.** Discover: `discover_plugins` (summary) → `yuzu://plugin-docs` (this page as data) → `discover_instructions` / `get_definition("crossplatform.software.inventory")`. Run: `execute_instruction {definition_id, parameters}`. Read: `/api/v1/responses/{id}` for `list`/`query`/`list_per_user`; `list_inventory`'s daily-sync output instead lands at `GET /api/v1/inventory/software`, since it carries no definition and is never dispatched through `execute_instruction`.
